propositions: Write-op parameter surfaces across lib/CLI/MCP adapters are hand-mirrored with no mechanical guard against drift; missing or divergent params are caught only by chance or LLM review.

A conformance oracle using a single shared contract table executes test cases through all three adapters against a fresh store and asserts identical accept/reject behavior for sanctioned params (force, reason, caused_by, ref, close_class).
Runtime conditional rules (close_class required for bug-close, reason required for certain classes) must be enforced consistently across all three adapters; violations are rejected identically.

Current MCP gaps (reason/caused_by/force not exposed on transition_ticket/claim_ticket per inputSchema) are captured as strict-xfail rows citing scratchy-leprous-galago, keeping the suite green in CI until those params are added.
Adapter-bound internals (source, return_alias, _creation_channel, repo_root) are excluded from the contract to avoid false divergence signals.
An in-suite simulated-parity test flips a strict-xfail row to xpass when a gap is closed, proving the oracle detects convergence and forces marker removal.
